title: Desk Guidance on Bringing an Agreement Current, Pauses, Extensions and Forfeiture — Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements
content:
# Arrears relief and forfeiture: desk guidance

A delinquent agreement of Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements is brought current by clearing the arrears, on the plans that admit reinstatement, and the plan's reinstatement fee is charged with it. An agreement is brought current only while it stands at delinquent or already current. Payments may be paused for the days the plan allows on the plans that admit a pause, and the final payment date moves out by the length of the pause. The term may be extended once by the plan's extension for the plan's extension fee on the plans that admit an extension, and a plan that admits none runs to its original date whatever the circumstances. An agreement that reaches the plan's forfeit threshold has the merchandise taken back and returns the plan's share of what the customer paid, and the plan that returns everything returns everything. The reinstatement charge and the extension charge are each booked to the agreement as their own entry under their own fee code, so an agreement that has been both reinstated and extended shows the two separately.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Matter | Condition | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bringing current | the plan admits reinstatement, the agreement stands at delinquent or current on its record, and the arrears are cleared | reinstatable | the agreement is brought current and the plan's reinstatement fee is charged with it, as its own entry |
| Bringing current | the agreement stands at opened, on hold, completed, forfeited or cancelled | not reinstatable | the agreement is not brought current |
| Pause | the plan admits a pause | pause available | payments are paused for no longer than the plan's longest pause, and the final payment date moves out by the length of the pause |
| Extension | the plan admits an extension and none has yet been taken | extension available | the term is extended once by the plan's extension days for the plan's extension fee, booked as its own entry |
| Extension | the plan admits none | no extension | the agreement runs to its original final payment date whatever the circumstances |
| Forfeit | the oldest unpaid payment reaches the plan's forfeit threshold | forfeited | the merchandise is taken back and the plan's share of what the customer paid is returned |

## The forfeit refund

The forfeit refund is the plan's forfeit share, as a percentage, of the total the customer paid on the agreement, the result carried to the cent. The total paid is the sum of every payment credited to the agreement over its whole life, from the day it was opened to the handling date, each taken at its full amount.

**On hypothetical figures.** Three payments of 300.00, 150.00 and 150.00 total 600.00; at a forfeit share of 70 percent the refund is 420.00. Payments totalling 433.33 at a share of 65 percent give 281.6645, carried to the cent as 281.66. On a plan whose forfeit share is 100 percent, the whole 600.00 is returned.
